note: A 2-acre Des Moines River access at St. Francisville, beside the Route B bridge to Iowa: a concrete boat ramp and a gravel lot, the only place to park. The area floods; do not drive onto flooded roads. --Claude
summary: DROP CANDIDATE (ramp-lot): page lists 'Designated Camping Sites' but the map (03/12) has no camping symbol (legend: boundary, roads, parking lot, boat ramp, forest), GIS has no camping point, and the only lot is the boat-ramp lot (the pin). Free/FCFS/no hookups/14 nights written manual in case it stays. Waterfront riverfront -> riverview if kept. Phone matches.
flags: DROP CANDIDATE (ramp-lot camping, MDC rule AWH 2026-11-09; precedents Cross Timbers, Dodd Access, Bird's Blue Hole): area page 'Things to Do When You Visit': 'Camping: Designated Camping Sites'; 'This area has a concrete boat ramp that provides access to the Des Moines River.' The area map (Conservation Commission (c) 03/12) legend is Boundary, Divided Highway, Paved Road, Gravel Road, Parking Lot, Boat Ramp, Forest - no camping symbol. GIS layer 27 has no camping point for area 6216; layer 26 has one lot (16, paved per GIS, gravel on imagery) at the pin. Imagery: a ~30 x 90 m gravel lot running down to the ramp at the river's edge, between the Route B bridge approach and woods; nothing else on the 2-acre area to camp on. With no designated point, the only place to camp is the boat-ramp lot -> drop.

WATERFRONT (if kept, riverfront -> riverview): the camping is the ramp lot itself; its north end meets the ramp ~25 m from the water and the pin is ~60-70 m from the river with the ramp and riverbank trees between. On-water needs an open apron within ~50 m with no road, ramp lot or beach between; a ramp lot is what lies between here.
FLOOD: page notice 'This area is subject to flooding. Check local conditions, and do not drive onto flooded roadways.' Put in the note.
Note rewritten: acreage kept only as size context, generic MDC text, the 14-day limit (now booking.max_stay_nights), 'site length not published' and directions dropped; flood caveat put in.
